Content:
In the diagram above, two tangents to the circle meet at the point [MATH: P.] The segments [MATH: \overline{AP}] and [MATH: \overline{BP}] are called tangent segments to the circle.

Content:
Note the following:

Content:
- Since [MATH: \overline{AP}] and [MATH: \overline{BP}] are tangent segments, we have that [MATH: \angle OAP] and [MATH: \angle OBP] are right angles.
- [MATH: \overline{OA}] and [MATH: \overline{OB}] are congruent because they are radii of the circle.
- [MATH: OP] is a common hypotenuse of [MATH: \triangle OAP] and [MATH: \triangle OBP.]

Content:
Therefore, [MATH: \triangle{OAP}] and [MATH: \triangle{OBP}] are also congruent by the HL (Hypotenuse-Leg) criterion.

Content:
[MATH: \triangle OAP \cong \triangle OBP]

Content:
As a consequence, we obtain
[MATH: AP = BP.]

Content:
To summarize, we have the following important property:

Content:
> Two tangent segments with a common endpoint in a circle's exterior are congruent.

sections.normalized_html: Given that [MATH: \overset{\longleftrightarrow}{PA}] and [MATH: \overset{\longleftrightarrow}{PB}] are tangents to the circle at [MATH: A] and [MATH: B,] respectively, what is the value of [MATH: z?]

[IMG: /graphics/2373b88661d8017b7bdf6e70b9fa9271]

Given that [MATH: \overset{\longleftrightarrow}{PA}] and [MATH: \overset{\longleftrightarrow}{PB}] are tangents to the circle at [MATH: A] and [MATH: B,] respectively, what is the value of [MATH: z?]

sections.normalized_html:
Since [MATH: \overset{\longleftrightarrow}{PA}] and [MATH: \overset{\longleftrightarrow}{PB}] are tangent to the circle, we have that

  • [MATH: m\angle{OAP}=m\angle{OBP}=90^\circ,] and

  • [MATH: \overline{OA} \cong \overline{OB}] are radii of the circle.

Therefore, [MATH: \triangle{OAP}] and [MATH: \triangle{OBP}] are congruent by HL (Hypotenuse-Leg): [MATH: \triangle OAP \cong \triangle OBP .]

As a consequence, the tangent segments [MATH: \overline{PB}] and [MATH: \overline{PA}] are congruent, and we obtain [MATH: PB|= PA; 5z + 2|= 12; 5z|= 10; z|= 2.]

The circle above touches the sides of the triangle at the points [MATH: A_1,] [MATH: B_1,] and [MATH: C_1.] Find the perimeter of [MATH: \triangle{ABC}.]

sections.normalized_html:
First, notice that [MATH: CA_1 = CB - BA_1 = 12 - 5 = 7\,\textrm{cm}.]

Now, since [MATH: \overset{\longleftrightarrow}{AB},] [MATH: \overset{\longleftrightarrow}{BC},] and [MATH: \overset{\longleftrightarrow}{AC}] are tangent to the circle, then we get three pairs of congruent tangent segments: [MATH: AB_1 \cong AC_1, \quad BA_1 \cong BC_1, \quad CA_1 \cong CB_1.]

As a consequence, [MATH: AB|= AC_{1} + BC_{1}; = 11 + 5; = 16cm,; AC|= AB_{1} + CB_{1}; = 11 + 7; = 18cm.]

Finally, the required perimeter is [MATH: p|= AB + BC + CA; = 16 + 12 + 18; = 46cm.]

sections.normalized_html: In the picture above, [MATH: \overset{\longleftrightarrow}{BC}] and [MATH: \overset{\longleftrightarrow}{BD}] are tangents to the circle at [MATH: C] and [MATH: D,] respectively. If [MATH: OD=3\,\textrm{cm},] what is the value of [MATH: OB?]

[IMG: /graphics/14523d95882cdb471a533f6a6f1e7a51]

In the picture above, [MATH: \overset{\longleftrightarrow}{BC}] and [MATH: \overset{\longleftrightarrow}{BD}] are tangents to the circle at [MATH: C] and [MATH: D,] respectively. If [MATH: OD=3\,\textrm{cm},] what is the value of [MATH: OB?]

sections.normalized_html:
Since [MATH: \overset{\longleftrightarrow}{BC}] and [MATH: \overset{\longleftrightarrow}{BD}] are tangent to the circle, then

  • [MATH: m\angle{OCB}=m\angle{ODB}=90^\circ,] and

  • [MATH: \overline{OC} \cong \overline{OD}] are radii of the circle.

Therefore, [MATH: \triangle{OCB}] and [MATH: \triangle{ODB}] are congruent by HL (Hypotenuse-Leg).

As a consequence, we obtain [MATH: m∠DBO|= m∠CBO; = (m∠DBC)/(2); = (60^{∘})/(2); = 30^{∘}.]

So [MATH: \triangle{ODB}] is a right [MATH: 30^\circ]-[MATH: 60^\circ]-[MATH: 90^\circ] triangle, and therefore its hypotenuse is twice the length of its shortest leg:

[MATH: OB = 2 \cdot OD = 2 \cdot 3 = 6 \,\textrm{cm}.]
